name: VA-10
label: Safe D

key_factors: Subramanyam's large fundraising edge ($1.17M vs $107K) and cash advantage
District's 6-point Democratic lean plus favorable national environment
Prediction markets price Democratic win at 95-97%
First-term incumbent with no polling or expert ratings available
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly Democratic: a D+6 district, an incumbent with a ten-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing the race at 95-97% Democratic. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict that picture, the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing Subramanyam under 55%, or significant outside spending against him, would warrant moving the race toward Likely D.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 10th District leans Democratic by about six points, and first-term incumbent Suhas Subramanyam is seeking re-election after winning the open seat in 2024. He has raised $1.17 million with $583,000 on hand, while Republican Dave Beckwith has raised about $107,000. Outside groups have spent modestly to support the incumbent and nothing against him. No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have published ratings for the race.

Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket price a Democratic win at roughly 95-97%. With a favorable district, a well-funded incumbent, and no evidence of a competitive race, the forecast treats the seat as safely Democratic, with uncertainty reflecting the absence of polling rather than any sign of vulnerability.
